text: Think from first principles, not by analogy.
Invert, always invert.
Carry a notebook everywhere. Write everything down.
Develop a latticework of mental models across many disciplines.
Sit with a problem long enough. Deep focus is a superpower.
Question every assumption, especially popular ones.
Read broadly and deeply, every day for life.
Update your beliefs when evidence changes. Never be the prisoner of your old conclusions.
Spend time thinking about thinking — your metacognition is your operating system.
Avoid the news. Study history instead.
Do the thing you're working on at the highest quality possible, always.
Work harder and longer than anyone else expects.
Embrace deep practice: isolate the hardest part and repeat it deliberately.
Master the fundamentals so completely they become instinct.
Finish what you start. Completion is rare and therefore valuable.
Show up every single day, especially when you don't want to.
Make enemies of distraction and comfort.
Seek the hardest challenges, not the easiest wins.
Say no to almost everything so you can say yes fully to the few things that matter.
Do your most important work when your mental energy is at its peak.
Know your enemy and yourself before every battle.
Move fast, hit where there is no defense, never where they are strongest.
Play long games with long-term people.
Preserve optionality. Never paint yourself into a corner.
Build systems, not goals.
Control the narrative. Whoever frames the story controls the outcome.
Use your opponent's strength against them.
source_figure: Judo principle, Sun Tzu, Genghis Khan

text: Concentrate your forces. Diluted effort produces diluted results.
Choose your battles. Not every fight is worth winning.
Spend less than you earn. Always. No exceptions.
Invest early and let compounding do the work.
Never lose money. Rule two: never forget rule one.
Understand what you own and why. Never invest in what you don't understand.
Create multiple streams of income. One source is a single point of failure.
Your network is your net worth. Invest in relationships obsessively.
Build assets that work while you sleep.
Pay yourself first. Automate savings before you have a chance to spend.
source_figure: Franklin, George Clason (The Richest Man in Babylon)

text: Know the difference between assets and liabilities — and only buy assets.
source_figure: Robert Kiyosaki's synthesis of Carnegie, Rockefeller

text: Give significantly. Generosity is both ethical and strategically wise.
Move your body every single day. Motion is medicine.
Sleep is performance. Protect it as a non-negotiable.
Eat to fuel performance, not for pleasure as a primary driver.
Train for both strength and endurance.
Avoid substances that dull the mind. Guard your cognitive clarity above all.
Cold exposure and physical hardship voluntarily sought toughens the mind.
Manage stress actively — it is the silent destroyer of health and performance.
Increase the demand on your body every week. Adaptation only comes from overload.
Maintain your range of motion deliberately. Stiffness is decay, not destiny.
Train toward a measurable target. A distance, a weight, a time. Vague effort produces vague results.
See a doctor for preventive care, not just when something breaks. Early detection expands your options.
Give your body recovery time after illness, grief, or prolonged stress. Pushing through depletes what rest alone restores.
Do what you say you will do. Integrity is the foundation of everything.
Take full ownership of your life. Stop blaming external circumstances.
Be brutally honest with yourself first, diplomatic with others.
Cultivate humility. The smarter you get, the more you know you don't know.
Never complain. Never explain. Deliver results and let your work speak.
Be kind. Not naive — kind. There is a difference.
Develop thick skin. Criticism is the price of doing anything significant.
Practice courage daily in small things to build it for large ones.
Forgive quickly — not for others, but for yourself.
Listen more than you speak. Most people do the opposite.
Surround yourself only with people who pull you up.
Make people feel genuinely seen and valued.
Choose your life partner as the most important strategic decision of your life.
Cut toxic people quickly and without guilt.
Mentor others and be mentored.
Never try to change someone's mind with argument alone. Change their environment or show them through action.
Repair relationships quickly. Unresolved conflicts compound like bad debt.
Identify the patterns you inherited from your family. Breaking a generational cycle is one of the most important things you will ever do.
Create and protect recurring rituals with family. Shared routines build the connective tissue that survives difficulty.
Set hard limits on work that bleeds into family time. No professional achievement compensates for sustained absence.
When a family member needs care, name who is responsible for what. Unspoken expectations around caregiving breed resentment.
Hold the same standards for family as for anyone else. Shared blood does not override the right to be treated with dignity.
Ask older family members about their lives while you still can. Those stories disappear the moment they do.
Friendships require maintenance. Reach out first, and do it before you need something.
Belong to something larger than your immediate circle. Community is the insurance that individual relationships cannot provide.
Initiate. Most people want more connection and are waiting for someone else to go first.
Steal from everywhere. Creativity is recombination.
Produce an enormous volume of work. Quality emerges from quantity.
Cross-pollinate disciplines. The best ideas live at intersections.
Protect your creative time. Schedule it first, non-negotiably.
Embrace constraints. Limitations force invention.
Incubate. Step away from a problem and let the unconscious work.
Pursue curiosity relentlessly, even when it seems irrelevant.
Embrace suffering as the forge. Every great person was built in the fire.
Fail fast, learn faster. Failure is data. Treat it as such.
Never let a crisis go to waste. Disruption creates windows that otherwise stay closed.
Build a reserve. Always have more runway than you think you need.
Detach your identity from outcomes. Do the work; release the result.
Play to win, but be prepared to lose everything and start again.
Develop a bias toward action. Motion defeats paralysis every time.
Find the thing only you can do and do it with everything you have.
Build something that outlives you. Make legacy the measure of success.
Define your values early, then let them make the hard decisions for you.
Serve something larger than yourself. Selfish lives feel hollow regardless of achievement.
Live as if this moment is both the first and last. Full presence is the rarest luxury.
Pick the work you would still do unpaid — obsession outlasts every paycheck.
Develop a daily practice of stillness — meditation, contemplation, or prayer.
source_figure: Marcus Aurelius, Pascal, Lao Tzu, Buddha

text: Accept what you cannot control with total equanimity.
Practice daily gratitude. It rewires perception at a fundamental level.
Contemplate your own mortality regularly. It clarifies everything.
source_figure: Marcus Aurelius (Memento Mori), Seneca, Samurai tradition

text: Non-attachment is not indifference — learn to act fully while holding outcomes lightly.
source_figure: Bhagavad Gita, Lao Tzu, Zen tradition

text: The inner world creates the outer world. Master yourself before trying to master anything else.
Design your day deliberately. Every unplanned hour will be filled by someone else's priorities.
Guard your attention like your life depends on it — because your life does.
Batch similar tasks. Context switching is the silent destroyer of productivity.
Rest is not the absence of work. It is part of the work.
Eliminate before you optimize. The best use of time is often not doing something at all.
Use the two-minute rule and the five-year test to filter decisions.
source_figure: Synthesis: Buffett's 25/5 rule, Bezos's regret minimization

text: Keep at least one hobby that exists only for enjoyment. Not every hour needs a return.
Schedule periods with no screens and no connectivity. The mind cannot restore itself in the same environment that depletes it.
source_figure: Henry David Thoreau, Ralph Waldo Emerson

text: Take vacations that fully disconnect you from work. Half-rest leaves you neither restored nor productive.
Keep one full day each week free of work. Unbroken rest is a discipline, not a reward.
Spend time outdoors without a destination or agenda. Nature restores attention and perspective that no indoor activity can replace.
Speak and write with clarity. If it can't be said simply, it isn't understood fully.
Tell stories. Data informs but stories move people to action.
Before persuading, understand the other person's position completely and charitably.
Write daily. Writing is thinking made visible and improvable.
Silence is a weapon. Use it deliberately.
Match your communication style to your audience, not to yourself.
To truly learn something, teach it. The gaps in your explanation are the gaps in your understanding.
Learn from the dead. Books give you access to the greatest minds across all time.
Apply what you learn immediately. Knowledge unused decays.
Be a beginner again in something every year. Novice mind sees what expert mind misses.
source_figure: Zen concept of Shoshin, da Vinci, Feynman

text: Build a personal curriculum and follow it with the discipline of a student and the curiosity of a child.
Learn from people who have done, not just those who have theorized.
Lead from the front. Authority is earned through demonstrated sacrifice and skin in the game.
Set the standard by your own example. What you tolerate becomes the culture.
Give credit generously. Take blame personally.
Know when to be the lion and when to be the fox.
Develop your people. The leader who builds other leaders multiplies their impact indefinitely.
Communicate the 'why' before the 'what' or 'how.' People will endure anything with a purpose.
Stay calm in chaos. The leader's emotional state is contagious.
You are your habits. The daily routine is the autobiography of a life.
Build your environment to make good behaviors automatic and bad ones difficult.
Win the morning. The first hour sets the tone for the day.
Never miss twice. Broken streaks are normal; giving up on the habit is the failure.
Track your habits. What is measured is managed and what is managed improves.
Stack new habits onto established ones. Never rely on motivation — rely on triggers.
source_figure: Franklin's routine structure, modern synthesis of ancient practice

text: Clear the clutter before you begin serious work. Disorder in the space becomes disorder in the mind.
source_figure: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Gustave Flaubert

text: Maximize natural light in the spaces where you live and work. Light is not decoration; it is a variable that governs your energy.
Protect your workspace from noise intrusion. Chronic background noise degrades focus and elevates stress.
Give every object in your home a fixed place. Time spent searching is a tax on everything else you do.
Design your workspace around the demands of your work. The space you work in shapes the quality of what you produce.
